label: PF Backlog 560
title: EPIC: CI/CD & Gates - SSOT doc + model + read API (PF + generated products)
body:
## Goal
One place to understand and read (via API) how PF builds/verifies/ships and how generated products do:
the CI/CD SSOT doc, a read-only model, and the read API for the orchestrator/UI.

## Children
- BI-PF-1238: CI/CD & Gates SSOT doc (done, PR#21).
- BI-PF-1239: CI/CD model + read API (this epic's build).

## Out of scope
Changing any gate behaviour; the future config-as-truth precheck refactor (Option C).

evidence:
Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=fc713aebf2a1
BLOCKER:
  - Diff delivers none of BI-PF-1243's AC: no CI/CD SSOT doc, no read-only model, no read/orchestrator API surface — only a flake fix for review-artifact ordering (test docstring even cites BI-PF-1531, not this item).
MAJOR:
  - `fix_guard.enforced` now silently skips enforcement for any item whose free-text `status` matches CLOSED_STATUSES, overriding an explicitly configured `enforce_items` entry — a gate-enforcement bypass with no validation, audit log, or entry in the approved design/contract.
  - The "newest review by `at`" selection is implemented twice (architect_review.py and fix_guard.py) with divergent semantics (sha-preferring vs mode-filtering); no single owner/helper, contrary to CL-001 and reuse expectations.
MINOR:
  - `architect_review._latest_review` behavior change has no regression test; only `fix_guard.latest_review` is covered, so the parallel ordering fix can drift unnoticed.
  - Lexicographic comparison of `at` strings misorders across formats ("Z" vs "+00:00", naive vs aware); records lacking `at` still fall back to mtime, so the original checkout-order flake persists for legacy artifacts.
  - No log/metric emitted when an item is skipped as closed or when ordering degrades to mtime — gate skips and ordering anomalies are not observable in production/CI.
  - Test IDs/docstring reference BI-PF-1531 rather than the reviewed item BI-PF-1243, weakening traceability.
NIT:
  - `tmp_path` fixture unused in `test_closed_item_is_not_enforced`.
  - Sentinel/initialization style (`best={}`/`key=None` vs `best_key=None`) differs between the two otherwise-identical loops.
SUMMARY:
  - The diff is a well-scoped tooling fix for non-deterministic review selection but does not implement the item's stated AC (SSOT doc + read-only model + read API), so the objective is unmet as submitted.
  - Top risks: status-based enforcement bypass not in the approved contract, duplicated ordering logic, and no coverage/observability for the architect_review path.
  - Language rule and test placement are compliant; recommend re-scoping the item or delivering the AC artifacts before approval.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present
